recent_posts.title: ToolJet low-code platform for building internal enterprise tools
recent_posts.summary: ToolJet is an AI-native low-code platform for building internal enterprise tools from plain-English prompts. It offers 80+ integrations (PostgreSQL, MySQL, REST APIs, Salesforce, etc.), self-hosting on every plan including a free Community Edition, and enterprise governance features. The platform targets engineering teams looking to ship internal tools faster without extensive custom development.

recent_posts.title: Becoming a Business Leader, Not Just a Technical One
recent_posts.summary: Senior technical leaders often hit a career ceiling not because of technical shortcomings, but because they fail to develop business fluency. A CTO mentor shares a framework of four moves — translate, trade-off, commit, and compound — to help technical executives think and communicate like business leaders. The post covers four practical contexts for building this fluency: understanding P&L and unit economics, engaging with sales and customers, participating in fundraising and investor relations, and contributing to strategy and resource allocation. The core argument is that the best thing a technical leader can do for their career is stop treating business knowledge as someone else's responsibility and start representing the business inside engineering.

recent_posts.title: The "Tech Pendulum"
recent_posts.summary: The tech industry repeatedly swings between opposing approaches — embedded vs. centralized teams, on-prem vs. cloud, monoliths vs. microservices, waterfall vs. agile. These pendulum swings happen because most approaches involve genuine trade-offs that take years to fully evaluate, and the technology landscape changes before any verdict is reached. Rather than chasing each trend, engineers and managers should observe the direction and position of current swings, prepare ahead of momentum shifts, and invest in durable skills like systems thinking, communication, and trade-off reasoning that remain valuable regardless of which way the pendulum moves.

recent_posts.title: Building Influence Within the Team
recent_posts.summary: A story-driven guide for engineering managers on how to build genuine influence within a team. Using a cautionary tale of a manager who failed by doing IC work and giving pep talks instead of driving real change, the post outlines practical tactics: modeling expected behavior, finding allies on the team, celebrating small wins, and avoiding common pitfalls like being a 'router manager' or being inconsistent. The core thesis is that all management is change management, and influence comes from enabling meaningful progress together rather than performing leadership.

recent_posts.title: Measure Less to Learn More: Using Fewer, Higher-quality Metrics to Capture What Matters
recent_posts.summary: Discord's data team shares how their Default Metric List grew uncontrollably over time, creating statistical problems. Having too many experiment metrics forces a tradeoff: unadjusted p-values produce false positives, while multiple hypothesis corrections reduce the ability to detect real changes. Their conclusion is that fewer, higher-quality metrics capturing distinct concepts outperform large metric sets, and they used simulations and Principal Component Analysis to find the right balance.

recent_posts.title: Claude Dispatch and the Power of Interfaces
recent_posts.summary: AI models are already highly capable, but chatbot interfaces create cognitive overhead that limits their usefulness — especially for less experienced workers. Research shows that chatbot-style interactions overwhelm users with walls of text and disorganized responses. Specialized interfaces like Claude Code exist for developers, but knowledge workers lack equivalent tools. Claude Cowork with Dispatch addresses this by letting users control a desktop AI agent from their phone via familiar messaging apps. Google is experimenting with profession-specific interfaces (Stitch, Pomelli, NotebookLM), while newer AI systems can generate on-demand interactive visualizations. The core argument: much of the perceived 'AI disappointment' stems from poor interfaces, not model limitations, and as interfaces improve, AI's true capabilities will become accessible to far more people.

recent_posts.title: Understanding systems
recent_posts.summary: Effective tutoring is primarily about motivation management and exposing flawed mental models. A good tutor selects exercises that reveal misconceptions, teaches students to verify their own solutions, and asks questions that guide students to discover answers themselves. This same approach — forming hypotheses about a system and deliberately testing them — applies universally: to debugging code, understanding networks, or learning any complex skill. The key insight is that learning happens through hypothesis formation and invalidation, not passive consumption of solutions.

recent_posts.title: Why the productivity system keeps you from what actually matters
recent_posts.summary: A reflective essay arguing that modern work systems are structurally designed to keep us busy with measurable, low-risk tasks while preventing us from reaching what truly matters. The author traces how factory-era time-shaped work evolved into knowledge work with infinite backlogs and gameable metrics, creating a productivity ratchet where efficiency gains never free up time but only raise expectations. Five costs are identified: guilt, neglect of important work, loss of the present, isolation, and atrophied attention. The author is skeptical that AI will break this cycle, calling it 'the disease dressed as the cure.' Practical suggestions include accepting the list is infinite, doing the important thing first, capping in-flight projects to three, and building purposeless time into the week.

recent_posts.title: The Gap Between How Your Team Sees You and How You See Yourself
recent_posts.summary: Engineering leaders often have a significant gap between how they see themselves and how their teams perceive them. Using a personal story about a Belbin team roles assessment, the author illustrates how self-perception can diverge from reality — in this case, seeing oneself as a Specialist while the team saw an Implementer. Practical tools to close this gap include asking specific feedback questions, requesting 360-degree reviews, and using personality assessments like DiSC or Big Five. The post also addresses why self-awareness is hard to develop: our self-image resists contradictory feedback. The recommended approach is to lean into discomfort, double down on strengths, and delegate weaknesses to others on the team.

recent_posts.title: How to be direct and strategic in high-stakes conversations
recent_posts.summary: Strategic communication is not manipulation — it's empathy in action. Before any high-stakes conversation, effective communicators consider what the other person already believes, what emotions the conversation may trigger, and how to open the discussion. A coaching example illustrates how reframing the same message by first understanding the manager's perspective turned a rejected idea into immediate buy-in. Being direct and being strategic are not opposites; thoughtful framing is what allows honesty to land.
